meta.source: Eskom hourly dataset ESK19679, calendar 2025. Per-unit series are measured output divided by that HOUR'S measured installed capacity.
meta.notes: demand=underlying(gross grid demand + est rooftop gen, app nets rooftop internally). wind_pu/solar_pu are per-unit of nameplate, so app energy = installed_MW*sum(pu).
meta.csp_source: Eskom normalised CSP feed-in (MW/MW), calendar year 2021, via PyPSA-RSA data/eskom_pu_profiles.csv. Replaces an earlier synthetic evening-shifted Gaussian which produced ZERO output before 10:00 - real SA CSP is already at ~50% by 09:00 because it runs off stored heat.
meta.wind_source_updated: CORRECTED 28 Aug 2026. The previous text here claimed wind_pu was a capacity-weighted MERRA-2 composite for calendar 2023. IT IS NOT, and was not. wind_pu is the Eskom Data Portal ESK19243 national metered series, rescaled by 0.8571 on 16 Aug 2026 to fix a nameplate error (3,466 MW understated the fleet; the series had to be rescaled so that installed_MW x sum(pu) still reproduced Ember's 11.6 TWh over the 4,142 MW Eskom meters). The result is a 31.97% capacity factor on a METERED basis. The capacity-weighted MERRA-2 composite for 2023, computed from nodal/profiles_regional_multiyear.json and the capacity split, is 37.70% - a MODELLED resource figure. The 0.848 ratio between them is reanalysis bias and is applied inside weatherYearNational() in index.html, not here. DO NOT reconcile these two numbers: they measure different things.
meta.solar_source_updated: Capacity-weighted composite from real regional profiles (Renewables.ninja MERRA-2, calendar year 2023), weighted by existing REIPPPP plant capacity per region from regional_renewable_capacity.json. Replaces the Eskom ESK19243 2025 national aggregate which used a single-point national profile.
meta.wind_nameplate_correction: Corrected 16 Aug 2026. wind_nameplate_est was 3466 MW, which understated the operating fleet, so wind_cf_2025 read 0.373 and every per-unit value was inflated by ~1.17x. The METERED ENERGY was always right - 3466 x 8760 x 0.373 = 11.33 TWh against Ember's 11.35 TWh for calendar 2025, agreeing to 0.2% - so only the divisor was wrong. Re-derived by requiring the series to reproduce Ember's 11.6 TWh (12 months to May 2026) over the 4,142 MW fleet Eskom actually meters (REIPPPP 4,042 + Eskom Sere 100). That solves to 4,044 MW, which lands on the REIPPPP wind fleet independently - a check on the method, not a fitted value. wind_pu was rescaled by 0.8571; total energy for a GIVEN fleet is unchanged, the per-unit normalisation is not. Do NOT add an availability or loss derate in the engine to compensate for this: these are metered profiles and already include availability, losses and real curtailment.
meta.basis: wind_pu and demand are METERED/observed. Do not mix with modelled MERRA-2 series without the bias correction - see wind_source_updated.
meta.rebuilt: 6 Sep 2026. Replaces a file that declared 2025 but contained 2023 data, and that divided by an estimated flat nameplate while capacity grew through the year - understating wind by 11% and solar by 21%.
meta.anchor_note: This file is OBSERVED. profiles_regional_multiyear.json is REANALYSIS. They describe the same fleet and year but by different methods, so they will not agree to 1% - the residual gap is the reanalysis bias, measured at about 5% for wind.

meta.demand_source: Built 26 Oct 2026 by build_demand_2026.py from ESK19679: RSA Contracted Demand less International Exports, calendar 2025 hourly shape; January-August scaled by 0.9534, the Jan-Aug 2026 vs Jan-Aug 2025 ratio of that domestic demand; September-December by 0.9766, August 2026 vs August 2025, plus the H1 2026 wheeled fleet (0.91 TWh), because those months of 2025 were already after the 2025 demand step. Rooftop added back at rooftopMW 8135.7 x derate 0.78, the engine formula, so the engine removes exactly this. Wheeled private output added back to the 2026 side of the ratio (1.03 TWh Jan-Aug 2026, 7 plants from COD; ratio 0.9442 before, 0.9534 after), because contracted demand omits load served by wheeled plant and the engine supplies it. Pre-2026 wheeled wind and solar (Msenge Emoyeni 69 MW, Selemela 2 and 3 200 MW, Damlaagte 97.5 MW, Castle 89 MW) added back on both sides: 0.964 TWh to the 2025 base, 1.146 TWh a year in 2026 (message 199 (3)). Domestic grid demand 194.62 TWh (2025) -> 188.82 TWh. Exports are added by the engine, not carried here. Provisional: re-run with full-year 2026.
meta.demand_2025_source: Built 26 Oct 2026 by build_demand_2026.py: ESK19679 calendar 2025 RSA Contracted Demand less International Exports, unscaled (194.62 TWh), rooftop added back at 6532 MW x derate 0.78 (2025, as modelled). Used when demandYear is 2025.
